claims.text: Grants cover tuition fees for undergraduate students at Scottish higher education institutions.
The grants are for students who are not eligible for government funding for their tuition fees.
There is a second-degree scheme for those reskilling in skills shortage areas.
The grants cover tuition fees up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover the cost of their tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
The fund will not accept an application if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR be able to demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain under a visa valid for the entire duration of the course, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds towards the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, unless seeking support for a second undergraduate degree.
Applicants eligible for a SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loan are expected to take full advantage of the loans available.
The fund will not consider an application if the applicant is eligible for support from Student Finance England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or any loan or grant from an overseas government or agency.
In general, the fund will not fund more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
Applications from students who previously received funding for an undergraduate degree and wish to start a different course may not be considered.
Part-time students receiving tuition fee support from SAAS may apply if the SAAS award is less than the total fees payable.
Students who came to Scotland solely to study at university or college without prior Scottish education or other ties to Scotland are not eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree level qualification may be considered exceptionally at the discretion of the fund.
For second degrees, applicants must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
For second degrees, applicants will enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
For second degrees, applicants must have been unable to gain employment in their previous degree subject, be unemployed, made redundant, or facing redundancy.
For second degrees, applicants must wish to reskill in a different field of study recognized as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026, for grants covering academic year 2026-27.
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
The fund considers household income and other extenuating circumstances.
In 2025-26, the median household income of award-holders was £10,000 per year.
All applications are made online.
The eligibility checker must be completed before applying.
Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student was informed of SAAS ineligibility after the portal closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks, provided all information and references are submitted promptly.
Supporting documents include evidence of eligibility, university acceptance letter, SAAS Award Notice, and P60 or pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
There is a 5MB size limit on each file submitted online.
